newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton envoy meets Netanyahu to open crisis talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton envoy meets Netanyahu to open crisis talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's Middle East peacemaker arrived in Israel on Wednesday to launch a new bid to revive talks paralysed by nearly two months of crisis.

As Dennis Ross began talks with Israeli premier Benjamin Netanyahu, neither Israeli or Palestinian officials held out much hope that he would be able to conjure up a breakthrough in the immediate future.
Ross, in his second shuttle mission within a month, met Netanyahu in closed-door talks in Jerusalem, Netanyahu aide Shai Bazak said. Bazak declined comment on the substance of the meeting.

The U.S. envoy had also been scheduled to travel to self-ruled Gaza for overnight talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat. A U.S. embassy spokesman said the meeting had been postponed until Thursday.
Prior to the envoy's arrival Israeli and Palestinian officials cautioned against hopes of an early breakthrough.

"Ross will have difficult talks with the Palestinians, since Arafat will reject any resumption of talks -- which were halted by Israel when it decided to build Har Homa (a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem) -- until the bulldozers stop working," said one PLO official.
Israeli-PLO talks broke down in March after Netanyahu gave the final go-ahead to construction of thousands of homes for settlers at a hilltop site the Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim.
Netanyahu aide David Bar-Illan said the work would go on.
"We obviously are not going to stop building in the settlements any more than the Palestinians are going to stop building in their towns," Bar-Illan said.
Israel has set a PLO crackdown on "terror" as its condition for resumed talks.

Ross's dogged shuttle diplomacy helped win the agreement under which Israel withdrew from most of the West Bank town of Hebron in January. However his last mission in April was overshadowed by a domestic Israeli crisis and failed to win a breakthrough.
Bar-Illan said that while "there seems to be movement every time Dennis Ross is around" it would be wrong to expect dramatic developments from his mission.
The envoy's visit follows Israeli President Ezer Weizman's meeting with Arafat on Tuesday at the Israel-Gaza border.

Weizman, who has taken on a mediation role in his largely ceremonial position as president, said Arafat had agreed to resume security coordination between the sides. But the Tuesday talks failed to budge the sides from their demands for ending seven weeks of crisis.

Western officials and Palestinian sources said the Clinton administration would refrain at this stage from asking Netanyahu to freeze the settlement work, instead requesting "positive steps" such as granting Jerusalem Palestinians building permits, and pushing forward plans for a Palestinian port and airport.
Settlers on Wednesday rebuilt a shack demolished a day earlier by Israeli police near the West Bank enclave of Yitzhar.
on Tuesday police forcibly removed dozens of settlers from a shack outside the Yitzhar settlement and destroyed it along with two other wooden structures they said were built illegally.
Several children who had been in the shack were slightly injured by broken glass and 18 settlers were arrested.
Israel captured the West Bank and Gaza in the 1967 Middle East War. More than 130,000 Israeli have since settled there amid some two million Palestinians.
